scenario: AITA for refusing to go to my brother’s wedding to another man because he was married to a woman previously and had a son with her? | Okay so stay with me. I’m 25 now and my older brother Chris got married when he was 27 to Taylor. Him and Taylor had a son the following year. They seemed to have a really good marriage but around when their son was 3, something happened. They spent a lot less time together and they eventually got a divorce. Well it came out that my brother confessed to Taylor that he was gay and had been “having feelings for another man.” They divorced after this and my brother started a new relationship with this man. This was three years ago and now Chris is marrying this same guy. The thing is, I’ve been witness to the devastation that this caused to his ex wife and son. He still is around for his son, but starting a life with a woman when he never was interested in women is something I’ll never understand. It’s not as if any of us would judge him for being gay. I’ve tried to help out with my nephew when I can so I’ve seen the confusion it’s caused him and the hurt it caused his ex, one of the kindest people I know. Now that he’s getting married again, the invitations have gone out and I’m invited. I really don’t feel like celebrating the harm that he caused his family by going to his wedding. I called him when I got the invitation and explained this to him and he started crying and saying that I wasn’t being fair and that he wants me to be there. I just explained that I couldn’t be there after everything that happened and I hung up. My sister called me and said that I was being an unfair dick and that I need to apologize to Chris and plan to be at the wedding. I told her what I told him. AITA for refusing to go? I think I’m being reasonable but my judgement is also clouded. Be honest.

Alex has tried to help out with the nephew but still feels conflicted about celebrating Chris's new marriage. Now, the question is whether Alex is being unreasonable (AITA) for refusing to attend the wedding. To determine this, I need to consider several factors: the emotional impact on the family, the right to personal boundaries, the importance of family unity, and the potential for healing or closure. First, the emotional impact: Chris's decision to come out as gay and leave his marriage caused significant pain for Taylor and the son. It's understandable that Alex feels hurt and betrayed, especially since Chris started a family with Taylor under the pretense of a heterosexual marriage. The fact that Chris is now remarrying to a man adds to the confusion and hurt, especially for the son who might not fully grasp the situation. On the other hand, everyone has the right to their own personal boundaries and to make decisions about what they feel comfortable participating in. Alex feels that attending the wedding would be celebrating the harm that was caused, which is a valid perspective. It's important to respect one's own feelings and limits, especially when it comes to family matters that have caused deep emotional wounds. However, family unity is also important. Weddings are significant events that often bring families together. By refusing to attend, Alex might be reinforcing the divide that already exists within the family. It could also be seen as punishing Chris for his past actions, which might not be fair, especially if Chris has shown willingness to make amends or work on the family relationships. Another angle to consider is the potential for healing or closure. Attending the wedding could be an opportunity for Alex to confront their feelings, communicate openly with Chris, and perhaps move towards reconciliation. It doesn't mean condoning Chris's past actions, but it could be a step towards healing for everyone involved. Additionally, it's important to recognize that Chris's decision to come out and marry his partner is a personal choice, and while it caused pain, it's also a part of who he is. It's possible that Chris is now in a happier and more authentic relationship, which could have positive effects on his well-being and, by extension, his ability to be a good father and family member. On the flip side, forcing Alex to attend the wedding could lead to more resentment and emotional strain. It's crucial to respect Alex's decision, even if others disagree with it. Family relationships are complex, and there's no one-size-fits-all solution. In conclusion, while there are valid arguments on both sides, it seems that Alex's decision to refuse attending the wedding is a personal choice based on their emotional well-being and the impact of Chris's actions on the family. It's not necessarily "right" or "wrong," but rather a decision that Alex feels is necessary for their own peace of mind. However, it's also important for Alex to communicate their feelings openly with Chris and the family to foster understanding and potentially work towards healing.
